1. Option A (C1C2C=C=C1C(C2C(=O)O)C(=O)O):

2. Option B (C1=C(C=C(C(=C1C=O)C=O)O)CO):

   - 13C NMR has some similarities but doesn't fully match
   - 1H NMR has a singlet at 2.09 for 3H (close to 2.35), but the aromatic pattern doesn't match well

4. Option D (CC(=O)OC1=CC=CC=C1C(=O)O):
   - 13C NMR matches very well with the given data (170.20, 169.60, 151.28, 134.64, 132.51, 124.01, 123.09, 122.26, 20.67)
   - 1H NMR has a singlet at 2.12 for 3H (close to 2.35), and aromatic protons in the 7-8 ppm range
   - The structure has a carboxylic acid group which would explain the broad IR peak at 2500-3200 cm⁻¹
   - The carbonyl groups (acetyl and carboxylic acid) would give IR peaks around 1753 and 1690 cm⁻¹

Option D (CC(=O)OC1=CC=CC=C1C(=O)O) is the best match for the given spectroscopic data. This is aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid), which has:
- An acetyl group (CH₃CO-) giving the 2.35 ppm singlet for 3H
- 4 aromatic protons in the 7.10-8.00 ppm range
- A carboxylic acid proton at 10.50 ppm
- The 13C NMR data matches very well
- The IR data is consistent with carboxylic acid (broad 2500-3200) and carbonyl groups (1753, 1690)
